_comment: Provenance + reproducibility manifest for the toolkit's REAL data sources. IMPORTANT: by default nothing here ships in the repo -- all of data/ and outputs/ are gitignored. 'local_file' is where an extract lives AFTER you build it locally (see data/README.md); it is NOT committed. Every dataset's fetch/build code lives in the notebook named in 'built_by' -- there is no separate build_*.py or fetch_*.py script anymore, and no separate _tmp_fetch/ cache; everything lands in data/. derived_extract entries carry a sha256/rows so verify_data.py can detect drift in your local build; live_fetch entries are not hash-checked because their source can legitimately change between runs (ClinVar updates ~weekly).
_publishable_comment: 'publishable' was added 2026-07-31 after re-verifying each dataset's redistribution terms; the per-dataset 'license' and 'publishable_note' fields below carry the reasoning. Values: 'yes' = permissive, safe to commit/host with attribution; 'noncommercial' = may be hosted by a strictly non-commercial tool with NC notice, but NOT committed to the public repo; 'no' = do not redistribute (ND, or redistribution unaddressed); 'confirm' = terms unresolved, treat as 'no' until checked.
ships_in_repo: data/publishable/ only: gnomAD, AlphaMissense, EVE, ClinVar (4 of 10 per-CFTR extracts). ESM1b, REVEL, PrimateAI, SpliceAI, Pangolin and CFTR2 are NOT redistributable — build them locally, see data/README.md.

gnomad_all.query: gene(gene_id: ENSG00000001626, reference_genome: GRCh38){ start stop variants(dataset: gnomad_r4){ variant_id hgvsc hgvsp consequence exome{ac an af filters} genome{ac an af filters} joint{ac an filters} } }
gnomad_all.version: gnomAD v4.1.1 (gnomad_r4), patch-released 2026-03-30 on the v4.1 exome+genome joint-calling release (2024-04-19).
gnomad_all.license: ODbL (Open Database License) + MIT terms; attribute gnomAD, keep-open, share-alike-under-ODbL, no reidentification. Verified 2026-07-31.
gnomad_all.note: NO PASS/AC filter applied -> 7577 CFTR variants (all consequence classes), incl. AC0-filtered; browser's default PASS+AC>0 view is smaller (see the funnel in tools/01, computed live from joint_filters -- not hardcoded). gnomad_af is gnomAD v4.1's joint (exome+genome combined) AC/AN, not max(exome_af, genome_af). Classified locally into gnomad_class (missense/noncoding/other_coding); gnomad_missense/gnomad_noncoding are in-memory filters over this one table via toolkit.py's load_gnomad_missense()/load_gnomad_noncoding(), not separate files. Publish frequency columns only; gnomAD's bundled SpliceAI annotation is CC BY-NC.

alphamissense.source: gs://dm_alphamissense/AlphaMissense_aa_substitutions.tsv.gz (protein-keyed bulk file, 216M rows genome-wide, streamed and filtered to UniProt P13569 -- switched 2026-08-07 from the similarly-named AlphaMissense_hg38.tsv.gz, which is genomic-SNV keyed and only reaches ~5.8 of the 19 possible alternate amino acids per residue via a single base change, undercounting true saturation; the protein-keyed file gives CFTR's exact 1,480x19=28,120 with zero gaps)
alphamissense.version: AlphaMissense v3 (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8208688, uploaded 2024-03-13; original v1 published 2023-09-19 alongside Cheng et al. 2023, PMID 37733863); filtered to UniProt P13569. GCS bucket URL has no version string, so the fetch cell records the live file's HTTP Last-Modified/ETag into data/alphamissense_cftr.release.json, exposed via load_alphamissense() as the am_release column.
alphamissense.license: CC BY 4.0 — DeepMind relicensed predictions from CC BY-NC-SA on 2024-03-13, lifting the NonCommercial restriction. Attribution required. Verified 2026-07-31.
alphamissense.note: am_class label text in this file is 'pathogenic'/'benign'/'ambiguous' (no 'likely_' prefix) -- same score and 0.340/0.564 cut-points as the hg38 file's 'likely_pathogenic'/'likely_benign' labels, just different label text.

clinvar.sha256: PENDING-rebuild (schema changed: now keeps every row + Type/ClinSigSimple; run verify_data.py --update after fetching)
clinvar.version: Pinnable: CLINVAR_RELEASE='latest' (default, dated via HTTP Last-Modified and recorded in data/clinvar_cftr.release.json) or a specific 'YYYY-MM' resolved to NCBI's monthly archive.
clinvar.license: CC0 1.0 / U.S. public domain; NCBI places no use/distribution restrictions, attribution requested, don't imply endorsement. Verified 2026-07-31.
clinvar.note: ClinVar updates ~weekly; every fetch records its resolved version into data/clinvar_cftr.release.json and the clinvar_release column. All CFTR/GRCh38 rows are kept (not just missense) -- includes VariationID, Name, Type, ClinicalSignificance, ClinSigSimple, ReviewStatus.
clinvar.publishable_note: SHIPPED in data/publishable/. CC0 1.0 / U.S. public domain — no redistribution restriction. The shipped copy is a point-in-time snapshot of a rolling weekly release; the exact version is pinned by the clinvar_release column and clinvar_cftr.release.json. Re-fetch for a current view.

cftr2.version: Release date is read from the workbook's own header and recorded in data/cftr2_cftr.release.json (currently '30 January 2026'). No historical archive exists on cftr2.org (checked) -- reproducing a past run means manually sourcing that older workbook yourself.
cftr2.license: CFTR2 Legal Terms & Conditions (cftr2.org/terms_of_use), §12 Intellectual Property: 'No portion of the Content may be reprinted, republished, modified, or distributed in any form without the express written permission of CFTR2, CFF, and Johns Hopkins', and separately prohibits creating derivative works; download permitted 'solely for your own non-commercial use'. Footer: 'clinical, research, and educational uses only. All other rights reserved.' Cite CFTR2. NB the expert-panel CALLS are separately available in ClinVar under CC0 — use that route if you need shareable CFTR2-derived classifications.
cftr2.publishable_note: DO NOT SHIP. Verified 2026-08-11 against cftr2.org Legal Terms & Conditions: §12 forbids republishing or distributing any portion of the Content and forbids creating derivative works without express written permission. data/cftr2_cftr.csv is BOTH a derivative work and a redistribution. Previously (incorrectly) marked 'yes' with no recorded justification. The CI gate in .github/workflows/smoke.yml blocks any tracked path matching 'cftr2_cftr'.

eve_cftr.version: EVE release label '2021-08' (CFTR = UniProt P13569). No live HTTP endpoint to date-check (manual zip download), so the build cell instead reads the zip's own embedded per-file timestamp for variant_files/CFTR_HUMAN.csv (zipfile.ZipInfo.date_time = 2021-07-08T21:00:44) into data/eve_cftr_2021-08.release.json, exposed via load_eve() as the eve_release column.
eve_cftr.license: MIT — confirmed 2026-08-07 on evemodel.org's Bulk Protein Data and Single Protein Data download pages, both stating verbatim: "The downloading of this data, and of all other data on this site, falls under the MIT License." Covers the scores themselves, not just the GitHub code (also MIT, copyright Pascal Notin 2021). No NC or ShareAlike restriction.

esm1b.version: ESM1b LLR, canonical UniProt P13569 (Brandes et al. 2023, PMID 37563329). No live HTTP endpoint to date-check (manual zip download), so the build cell instead reads the zip's own embedded per-file timestamp for content/ALL_hum_isoforms_ESM1b_LLR/P13569_LLR.csv (zipfile.ZipInfo.date_time = 2022-05-06T05:28:04) into data/esm1b_cftr.release.json, exposed via load_esm1b() as the esm1b_release column.
esm1b.license: Scores CC BY-NC 4.0 (HuggingFace Space ntranoslab/esm_variants, declared license); the ntranoslab/esm-variants GitHub code is MIT. Cite Brandes et al. 2023, Nat Genet, PMID 37563329.
esm1b.publishable_note: DO NOT SHIP in this MIT repo. Resolved 2026-08-11: the ntranoslab/esm-variants GitHub repo is MIT, but that MIT text scopes to 'the Software'. The artifact this build actually reads (ALL_hum_isoforms_ESM1b_LLR.zip) is distributed by the HuggingFace Space ntranoslab/esm_variants, whose declared license is CC BY-NC 4.0. NC data inside an MIT-licensed repo is an incompatible pair — same reasoning as SpliceAI. A strictly non-commercial tool may host it with attribution.

revel.version: REVEL v1.3, GRCh38 (Ioannidis et al. 2016, PMID 27666373). No live HTTP endpoint to date-check (manual zip download), so the build cell instead reads the zip's own embedded per-file timestamp for its one member, revel_with_transcript_ids (zipfile.ZipInfo.date_time = 2021-05-03T15:50:38), into data/revel_cftr_v1.3.release.json, exposed via load_revel() as the revel_release column.
revel.license: free for NON-COMMERCIAL use (contact authors otherwise)
revel.publishable_note: Grants USE, not redistribution — republishing is unaddressed. Do not host or commit. Email the REVEL authors for redistribution permission, or query dbNSFP/live sources at request time.
revel.note: local_file has 10,826 raw rows (all CFTR transcripts REVEL scored) plus an ensembl_transcriptid column added 2026-08-07; load_revel() filters to only the 9,730 rows tagged with CFTR's canonical transcript (ENST00000003084) -- verified against live Ensembl VEP that the other 1,096 rows (transcript ENST00000468795, CDS-start-unconfirmed per Ensembl) don't match current annotation at all (0/1096) and aren't a reliable second opinion.

primateai.source: Illumina BaseSpace https://basespace.illumina.com/s/cPgCSmecvhb4 (PrimateAI native release, v0.2, hg38)
primateai.version: PrimateAI (Sundaram et al. 2018, PMID 30038395), native release v0.2 hg38. No live endpoint to date-check (manual download), so the build cell reads the gzip file's own MTIME header field directly (2018-09-04T21:19:43+00:00) into data/primateai_cftr.release.json, exposed via load_primateai() as primateai_release. Switched 2026-08-08 from dbNSFP's ClinVar-associated subset (~1,976 rows, ~20% of CFTR's true missense universe) to this native release: 9,722 of CFTR's 9,730 true possible missense SNVs (verified in the revel entry), scored under a single confirmed-canonical UCSC transcript (uc003vjd = ENST00000003084). Verified byte-identical scores against the old dbNSFP subset wherever they overlap (correlation 1.0).
primateai.license: "For research use only" (Illumina, 2018, stated verbatim in the release file's own header) -- more specific than a generic non-commercial note.
primateai.publishable_note: Research-use-only is a real redistribution blocker, independent of the earlier dbNSFP ND concern. To include PrimateAI, obtain permission from Illumina, or query a live source at request time.

spliceai.built_by: tools/07_spliceai.ipynb (build cell; manual VCF download, .tbi seek)
spliceai.raw_source: spliceai_scores.masked.snv.hg38.vcf.gz (~26.6 GB) + spliceai_scores.masked.indel.hg38.vcf.gz (~64.1 GB) — both external, not committed. The build cell falls back to the raw file of either class if the masked one is missing or zero-byte, and records score_type per row.
spliceai.source: Illumina BaseSpace share https://basespace.illumina.com/s/otSPW8hnhaZR ('Predicting splicing from primary sequence' / genome_scores_v1.3)
spliceai.version: SpliceAI precomputed v1.3, GRCh38. Reporting distance: the public README (github.com/Illumina/SpliceAI) documents the CLI flag -D 'maximum distance between the variant and gained/lost splice site (default: 50)' but does NOT state which parameters the precomputed downloads were generated with -- the files settle it themselves, since their DP_* delta positions span exactly -50..+50 across all 566,106 CFTR SNVs and hit the boundary in 34,779 of them, which is only consistent with -D 50. The Gencode v24 annotation is from the SpliceAI publication, not from anything in the files; treat it as a citation rather than a verified property of this download. No live endpoint to date-check, but the VCFs state their own version in their headers -- the build cell reads ##fileDate (20191004 -> 2019-10-04), ##reference (GRCh38/hg38) and the SpliceAI annotation version named in the ##INFO line (SpliceAIv1.3) from the files it actually used, into data/spliceai_cftr_2021_v1.3.release.json, exposed via load_spliceai() as the spliceai_release column. Uniformly MASKED: 566,106 SNVs + 1,509,624 indels, both from the masked releases, per Illumina's recommendation for variant interpretation. Rows still carry score_type/variant_class because the build cell falls back to the raw file of a missing class. Re-verified 2026-08-12 with all four files downloaded, joining masked to raw on coordinate across all 2,075,730 records: masking is all-or-nothing (0 partial changes) and one-directional (raw >= masked, 0 violations) in BOTH variant classes; DS_max agrees exactly on 95.48% (SNVs 95.84%, indels 95.35%; mean |diff| 0.0021); 450 records cross the 0.5 HIGH cut (113 SNVs + 337 indels, all in the same direction), but that is 1 of the 4,535 observed gnomAD non-coding variants (c.2013A>G) and 0 of the 1,728 scored CFTR2 variants — do not compare a masked score against a raw one.
spliceai.license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (Jaganathan et al. 2019, PMID 30661751) — attribute SpliceAI+Illumina; do NOT commit raw VCF; publishing derived extract needs NC notice (plan R43)
spliceai.publishable_note: CC BY-NC: a strictly non-commercial tool may serve it with attribution + NC notice; do NOT commit to the public repo. Alternative: query the Broad SpliceAI lookup API live instead of hosting the extract.
spliceai.note: All four raw deltas (DS_AG/DS_AL/DS_DG/DS_DL) are kept alongside the derived spliceai_ds_max, so the headline collapse is reversible and the *type* of splice change stays readable. The `symbol` column carries the gene the release annotated each score against, so the CFTR filter is auditable rather than assumed.

pangolin.reproducibility_note: Rebuilt 2026-08-15 under torch 2.13.0+cpu and confirmed against the previous build: same 1,892 scored / 2,097 targets, same tier counts (1,518 LOW / 114 MODERATE / 260 HIGH), same scores for all five panel alleles. 16 of the 1,892 differ by exactly 1 unit in the 4th decimal place (e.g. 0.0082 -> 0.0081), all of them multi-base indels, none anywhere near a 0.2/0.5 cut. So Pangolin scores here are reproducible to ~3 dp but not bit-for-bit across torch builds/devices -- which is precisely why the release stamp records torch_version and device alongside the weight hashes, and why the sha256 above pins one specific run rather than 'the' answer.
pangolin.built_by: tools/08_pangolin.ipynb (build cell; runs the model locally)
pangolin.raw_source: Pangolin model weights bundled in the pip package + data/cftr_region_grch38.fa (~215 kb CFTR region, Ensembl GRCh38); no whole-genome download
pangolin.version: Pangolin (Zeng & Li 2022, Genome Biol 23:103, PMID 35449021). This is the only entry here that is a MODEL RUN rather than a download, so the release stamp records TWO things, which answer different questions. (1) The MODEL'S RELEASE -- Zeng & Li 2022 -- is the temporal anchor: it bounds what could have informed the model, which is what makes a hold-out by first-report date meaningful when the score is later used as evidence (see TOOL_YEAR in toolkit.py and the circularity discussion in tools/05 section 2). (2) The RUN PROVENANCE -- pangolin package version, SHA-256 of the twelve models/final.*.3.v2 weight files loaded, torch version and device, the Ensembl reference region, and the scope -- is what a rerun must match to reproduce a score. Both go into data/pangolin_cftr.release.json, exposed via load_pangolin() as the pangolin_release column, and both are written WHILE the model runs because neither survives in a finished CSV. An extract built before release tracking existed reports 'unknown' rather than a reconstructed guess; to stamp it, delete data/pangolin_cftr.csv and rerun the build cell.
pangolin.note: Model output you generated yourself (better footing than redistributing a licensor's table), but the model license is non-commercial — a strictly non-commercial tool may host it with citation; do NOT commit to the public repo. No precomputed Pangolin release has been found, and it is not carried in dbNSFP, so running the model is the only route to scores rather than a fallback. Default scope (SCOPE = "cftr2") runs it over the CFTR2 list: 2,097 rows, 1,893 with GRCh38 coords, 1,892 scored, SNVs AND indels. SCOPE = "curated" scores only the 5 classic CF splice alleles as a fast install check. BOTH are source=REAL: a narrower scope is less coverage, not less real output, and DEMO in this repo means hand-authored illustrative numbers (the earlier 'label follows coverage' rule mislabelled real model output as DEMO and has been dropped). Unscorable rows are kept with a skip_reason (204 lack CFTR2 coords; 1 event >100 bp). pangolin_score is a COLLAPSE -- max(gain, |loss|) over the +/-50 bp window -- so unlike SpliceAI's retained deltas the direction of the change is not recoverable from the extract. NB Pangolin is NOT architecturally independent of SpliceAI: per Zeng & Li 2022, 'Pangolin's architecture resembles that used in SpliceAI' (same 16 dilated residual blocks, same ~10 kb receptive field; verified against pangolin/model.py, whose L/W/AR match SpliceAI-10k), differing in the output layer and in supervision (quantitative splice-site usage across 4 species and 4 tissues vs SpliceAI's binary annotated-site target). Agreement between the two is partial corroboration, not two independent votes -- treat accordingly in any cross-tool benchmark. The sha256/rows here identify the exact extract tools/08's committed outputs were produced from; note verify_data.py hashes only 'derived_extract' entries, so for this 'model_run' entry they are provenance rather than an enforced check.

cadd.version: CADD v1.7 (GRCh38), released 2024-01-05 — Schubach et al. 2024, Nucleic Acids Research 52(D1):D1143, PMID 38183205, doi 10.1093/nar/gkad989. CORRECTED 2026-08-15: this entry previously cited Rentzsch et al. 2021 (PMID 33618777) for v1.7, but that paper is CADD-Splice = v1.6; the v1.7 release notes open by describing what changed 'Since the CADD v1.6 release in 2021'. v1.7 added ESM-1v protein language model scores, a regulatory CNN over open-chromatin regions, and Zoonomia (241-mammal) conservation. There is no file to hash: the version pinned in the URL is the only anchor, and tools/09 returns it alongside every score.
cadd.note: Queried live per-variant; cache responses to make reproducible. Do NOT cache-and-republish (CADD has separate academic/commercial terms). NOT trained on clinical labels — the v1.7 release notes describe contrasting >14M human-lineage-derived variants (proxy-neutral) against a size-matched simulated set (proxy-deleterious) — so DIRECT ClinVar circularity is low. But CADD is a META-MODEL and this toolkit is inside it: the v1.7 feature table lists 'Masked SpliceAI' acceptor/donor gain/loss scores (the same masked flavour tools/07 builds), MMSplice features, and ESM-1v scores (a sibling of tools/04's ESM1b). So CADD agreeing with SpliceAI or ESM1b is partly the same evidence counted twice — do not treat them as independent votes in a benchmark. At 2024 it is also the most recently released tool covered here, giving it the widest window in which a variant could already have been well-characterised.
